newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks soar to fifth straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks soar to fifth straight record close.

text.p: * Toronto stocks soared to their fifth straight record finish on Wednesday * TSE 300 hit new intraday high of 6746.18 * TSE posted gains in all 14 sub-groups * 102 million shares traded.
Toronto stocks rallied to their fifth consecutive record close on Wednesday, buoyed by favorable earnings and moderate inflation data, analysts said.
The TSE 300 Composite Index jumped 88.89 points to 6744.81 in heavy turnover of 102 million shares worth C$1.8 billion.
The key index also set an intraday high of 6746.18.

"The economy continues to expand and earnings have been quite solid. Stocks have continued to move up because nothing has been reported that would cause concern," said Subodh Kumar, chief strategist for CIBC Wood Gundy. In New York, the Dow Jones Industrial Average broke through the 8,000 barrier.

Canadian stocks and bonds strengthened on U.S. consumer price data that showed minor inflationary pressures on the U.S. economy. Early Canadian earnings reports also lifted Canadian stocks, particularly in cyclical issues.
"When you look at companies like Falconbridge and Alcan (Aluminium Ltd), the earnings have been good," Kumar said.
Banking, utilities and other interest rate sensitive stocks led gains in Toronto's 14 sub-groups. Advancing stocks outpaced declines 556 to 460 with 273 issues unchanged.
Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce rose 1.05 to 37.70. Bank of Montreal, which urged the federal government to allow bank mergers on Wednesday, rose 1.20 to 57.70.

* Crystallex International Corp sank 4.20 to close at 3.80 on 3.4 million shares after Venezuela's Supreme Court ruled on the company's dispute with Placer Dome Inc over the Las Cristinas gold property.
* Golden Rule Resources Corp dropped 1.16 to 1.04 after the company said earlier promising assays from its Ghana gold project were unreliable.
